subject: Demo request: Dedicated capacity for throughput-sensitive text generation (ClarifyAI)
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@clarityai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo request: Dedicated capacity for throughput-sensitive text generation

Hi Marissa,

We just completed the self-serve sign-up and indicated interest in a Dedicated capacity demo with Redwood. Our product team is evaluating inference economics for a high-throughput use case and we need to understand latency guarantees and burst behavior. Quick summary of our expected workload: 
- Typical steady-state: ~500 QPS (inference requests/minute equivalent traffic)
- Peak bursts: up to ~1,200 QPS for 5–15 minutes
- Average prompt length: ~64 tokens; responses average ~120 tokens
- Target p95 latency: <= 200–300ms for short prompts

We'd like to schedule a 45-minute technical walkthrough with an engineer who can discuss batching, autoscale behavior, and any recommended quantization/architecture profiles. Also important: we need an initial answer on compliance—SOC2 and data retention defaults.

Available times this week (PST): Thu 10:00–12:00, Fri 09:00–11:00.

I've attached a small sample-of-traffic CSV. Can you confirm next steps?

Thanks,
Sofia
VP Product | ClarifyAI
attachment: clarity_sample_traffic.csv (csv, 12KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo request: Dedicated capacity for throughput-sensitive text generation

Hi Sofia — thanks for the details and for uploading the sample traffic. Ben and Diego are looped in from Solutions and Capacity so we can pair on the call. Quick questions before we lock a slot:
- Are your QPS numbers steady per endpoint or aggregated across many endpoints?
- Do you expect concurrent long-running generation requests (>=1k tokens) or mostly short ones?
- Any strict region requirement (we have eu/us/apac pools)?

We can do Thu 10:30 PT or Fri 09:30 PT — which works best for you? We'll prepare a short runbook (batching, warmup, autoscale thresholds) and bring a dedicated infra engineer to talk about warm pools and KV cache reuse. Also, we can bring a member of our Security team for a 10-minute compliance overview if Procurement wants to join.

If you prefer, we can send a HubSpot meeting link and an invite (will include an .ics).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — those times work. To answer: the QPS numbers are aggregated across 3 main model endpoints (routing layer) but 75% of traffic hits a single endpoint. We rarely do very long generations in production; typical responses are <200 tokens. Bursts are traffic-driven (user events) rather than scheduled. Region: US preferred.

Procurement is looping in the security questionnaire — I've attached an initial PDF of items they usually ask about. For the call, please bring a quick outline of SLAs for Dedicated (latency targets, failover behavior) and any recommended settings for autoscale and pre-warmed capacity.

Confirm Thu 10:30 PT for now — send the invite and HubSpot link.

Appreciate it,
Sofia
